usual_baseline: Overall compliance runs at about 64–70% [2107, 2361]. Pre-operative and intra-operative elements are usually done well. Post-operative elements lag: opioid avoidance only 7.9–8% [2107, 2352], nutritional drinks 0–44.3% [2677, 2352], and routine drains, NG tubes and bowel preparation persist. Mean stay 5.5–9.8 days at baseline.
fix_that_works: An ERAS proforma: in notes 0% to 92%, anti-emetics 32% to 100%, stay 5.5 to 3.75 days [2477]. Overall adherence 63.9% to 81.1%, stay 9.8 to 7.1 days [2361]. A discharge checklist: median stay 5 to 4 days, day 1 catheter removal 63% to 80% [2632]. Nutritional work: supplements 0% to 75% [2677]. MDT protocol: regular medicines 37% to 62% [2749].
fix_that_fails: Opioids stayed at 100% after an action plan; drains (85%) and NG tubes (80%) remained high [2811]. Day 1 trial without catheter reached only 50% [2477]. Physiotherapy referral fell from 100% to 85% [2677].
consultant_advice: Don't audit the whole ERAS bundle again; the pre-operative parts are fine. Pick one post-operative element that stays poor, such as opioid avoidance, drains or nutrition drinks, and link it to length of stay, which several audits showed can fall.
